sanskrit: tāṃ kathām ilasaṃbaddhāṃ rāmeṇa samudīritām lakṣmaṇo bharataś caiva śrutvā paramavismitau
english: Having heard that tale connected with Ilā, as narrated by Rāma, both Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata were filled with the utmost wonder.

sanskrit: tau rāmaṃ prāñjalībhūtvā tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ vistaraṃ tasya bhāvasya tadā papracchatuḥ punaḥ
english: With folded hands they asked Rāma once more to tell them in full detail about the nature of that great-souled king's condition.

sanskrit: kathaṃ sa rājā strībhūto vartayām āsa durgatim puruṣo vā yadā bhūtaḥ kāṃ vṛttiṃ vartayaty asau
english: How did that king endure his wretched state when he had become a woman? And when he became a man again, how did he conduct himself?

sanskrit: tayos tad bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā kautūhalasamanvitam kathayām āsa kākutṣṭhas tasya rājño yathā gatam
english: Hearing their words, filled as they were with eager curiosity, Kākutstha narrated the full course of that king's story just as it had unfolded.

sanskrit: tam eva prathamaṃ māsaṃ strībhūtvā lokasundarī tābhiḥ parivṛtā strībhir ye 'sya pūrvaṃ padānugāḥ
english: During that very first month, having become a woman of surpassing beauty, she wandered surrounded by those followers of hers who had likewise become women.

sanskrit: tat kānanaṃ vigāhyāśu vijahre lokasundarī drumagulmalatākīrṇaṃ padbhyāṃ padmadalekṣaṇā
english: The woman of incomparable beauty, her eyes like lotus petals, plunged swiftly into that forest thick with trees, shrubs, and creepers, and roamed it on foot.

sanskrit: vāhanāni ca sarvāṇi saṃtyaktvā vai samantataḥ parvatābhogavivare tasmin reme ilā tadā
english: Having abandoned all her mounts on every side, Ilā took her pleasure in the hollow of that mountain's broad flank.

sanskrit: atha tasmin vanoddeśe parvatasyāvidūrataḥ saraḥ suruciraprakhyaṃ nānāpakṣigaṇāyutam
english: Then, in that woodland region not far from the mountain, she beheld a lake of wondrous beauty, thronged with flocks of birds of every kind —

sanskrit: dadarśa sā ilā tasmin budhaṃ somasutaṃ tadā jvalantaṃ svena vapuṣā pūrṇaṃ somam ivoditam
english: — and there in that lake Ilā saw Budha, the son of Soma, blazing with his own radiance like the full moon when it rises.

sanskrit: tapantaṃ ca tapas tīvram ambhomadhye durāsadam yaśak saraṃ kāmagamaṃ tāruṇye paryavasthitam
english: He was performing fierce austerities within the water, unapproachable, moving at will, standing in the full bloom of his youth.

sanskrit: sā taṃ jalāśayaṃ sarvaṃ kṣobhayām āsa vismitā saha taiḥ pūra puruṣaiḥ strībhūtai raghunandana
english: Astonished, she stirred the entire lake into commotion together with those former men who had become women, O joy of the Raghu lineage.

sanskrit: budhas tu tāṃ nirīkṣyaiva kāmabāṇābhipīḍitaḥ nopalebhe tadātmānaṃ cacāla ca tadāmbhasi
english: But Budha, gazing upon her and pierced by the arrows of desire, lost command of himself at that moment and trembled in the water.

sanskrit: ilāṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sa trailokyābhyadhikāṃ śubhām cintāṃ samabhyatikrāmat kā nv iyaṃ devatādhikā
english: Gazing upon the radiant Ilā, who surpassed in beauty even the goddesses of the three worlds, he fell into deep thought: "Who is this being who exceeds even the divine?"

sanskrit: na devīṣu na nāgīṣu nāsurīṣv apsaraḥsu ca dṛṣṭapūrvā mayā kā cid rūpeṇaitena śobhitā
english: "I have never before seen anyone — not among the goddesses, not among the Nāgī women, not among the Asura women, not even among the Apsarases — adorned with this beauty."

sanskrit: sadṛśīyaṃ mama bhaved yadi nānyaparigrahā iti buddhiṃ samāsthāya jalāt sthalam upāgamat
english: "She would be a fitting match for me, if she belongs to no other." Settling his mind on this resolve, he came up from the water onto the bank.

sanskrit: sa āśramaṃ samupāgamya catasraḥ pramadās tataḥ śabdāpayata dharmātmā tāś cainaṃ ca vavandire
english: Having come to the hermitage, the righteous-souled one called out to four of the women; they, in turn, paid homage to him.

sanskrit: sa tāḥ papraccha dharmātma kasyaiṣā lokasundarī kimartham āgatā ceha satyam ākhyāta māciram
english: The righteous one asked them: "Whose is this woman of incomparable beauty? For what purpose has she come here? Tell me the truth without delay."

sanskrit: śubhaṃ tu tasya tadvākyaṃ madhuraṃ madhurākṣaram śrutvā tu tāḥ striyaḥ sarvā ūcur madhurayā girā
english: Hearing those words of his, auspicious and sweet, with syllables gentle as honey, all those women replied in equally sweet voices.

sanskrit: asmākam eṣā suśroṇī prabhutve vartate sadā apatiḥ kānanānteṣu sahāsmābhir aṭaty asau
english: "This fair-hipped one is always our mistress and our lord. She has no husband; she roams the forest glades with us."

sanskrit: tad vākyam avyaktapadaṃ tāsāṃ strīṇāṃ niśamya tu vidyām āvartanīṃ puṇyām āvartayata sa dvijaḥ
english: Hearing those words of the women, whose meaning was unclear, that twice-born one mentally recited the holy recollective spell called Āvartanī.

sanskrit: so 'rthaṃ viditvā nikhilaṃ tasya rājño yathāgatam sarvā eva striyas tāś ca babhāṣe munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Having thereby learned the full truth of the king's story just as it had come about, the foremost of sages addressed all those women.

sanskrit: atra kiṃ puruṣā bhadrā avasañ śailarodhasi vatsyathāsmin girau yūyam avakāśo vidhīyatām
english: "Were men, O fortunate ones, dwelling on the slope of this mountain? You shall remain on this mountain; let a dwelling be prepared."

sanskrit: mūlaputraphalaiḥ sarvā vartayiṣyatha nityadā striyaḥ kimpuruṣān nāma bhartṝn samupalapsyatha
english: "You shall all live always on roots, fruit, and bulbs; and you women shall obtain as husbands beings known as Kiṃpuruṣas."

sanskrit: tāḥ śrutvā somaputrasya vācaṃ kiṃpuruṣīkṛtāḥ upāsāṃ cakrire śailaṃ bahvyas tā bahudhā tadā
english: Hearing the words of the son of Soma, those many women, transformed into Kiṃpuruṣī females, thenceforth attended upon that mountain in many different ways.

sanskrit: śrutvā kimpuruṣotpattiṃ lakṣmaṇo bharatas tadā āścaryam iti cābrūtām ubhau rāmaṃ janeśvaram
english: Having heard the origin of the Kiṃpuruṣas, both Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata exclaimed "How wonderful!" to Rāma, lord of the people.

sanskrit: atha rāmaḥ kathām etāṃ bhūya eva mahāyaśāḥ kathayām āsa dharmātmā prajāpatisutasya vai
english: Then Rāma of great renown, righteous of soul, once more narrated this tale about the son of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: sarvās tā vidrutā dṛṣṭvā kiṃnarīr ṛṣisattamaḥ uvāca rūpasaṃpannāṃ tāṃ striyaṃ prahasann iva
english: Seeing all those women flee, that best of sages addressed the woman endowed with incomparable beauty, almost as if smiling.

sanskrit: somasyāhaṃ sudayitaḥ sutaḥ surucirānane bhajasva māṃ varārohe bhaktyā snigdhena cakṣuṣā
english: "I am the beloved son of Soma, O fair-faced one; worship me, O beautiful-limbed woman, with devoted and tender eyes."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā śūnye svajanavarjitā ilā suruciraprakhyaṃ pratyuvāca mahāgraham
english: Hearing his words, abandoned by her own people and alone in that wilderness, Ilā answered that great luminary of wondrous splendor.

sanskrit: ahaṃ kāmakarī saumya tavāsmi vaśavartinī praśādhi māṃ somasuta yathecchasi tathā kuru
english: "I am free to act as I will, O gentle one; I am under your power. Command me, O son of Soma; do with me as you desire."

sanskrit: tasyās tad adbhutaprakhyaṃ śrutvā harṣasamanvitaḥ sa vai kāmī saha tayā reme candramasaḥ sutaḥ
english: Hearing those words of hers, so wondrous in their tenor, the son of the Moon, filled with joy and consumed by love, sported with her.

sanskrit: budhasya mādhavo māsas tām ilāṃ rucirānanām gato ramayato 'tyarthaṃ kṣaṇavat tasya kāminaḥ
english: For Budha the month of Mādhava passed like an instant, as he delighted exceedingly with that bright-faced Ilā, so great was his passion.

sanskrit: atha māse tu saṃpūrṇe pūrṇendusadṛśānanaḥ prajāpatisutaḥ śrīmāñ śayane pratyabudhyata
english: Then, when the month was complete, the glorious son of Prajāpati, his face like the full moon, awoke upon his bed.

sanskrit: so 'paśyat somajaṃ tatra tapyantaṃ salilāśaye ūrdhvabāhuṃ nirālambaṃ taṃ rājā pratyabhāṣata
english: He saw Budha, the son of Soma, there performing austerities in the lake, arms raised, unsupported; and the king addressed him.

sanskrit: bhagavan parvataṃ durgaṃ praviṣṭo 'smi sahānugaḥ na ca paśyāmi tat sainyaṃ kva nu te māmakā gatāḥ
english: "Revered one, I entered a difficult mountain together with my retinue, but I cannot see that army. Where have those who belong to me gone?"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tasya rājarṣer naṣṭasaṃjñasya bhāṣitam pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ sāntvayan parayā girā
english: Hearing those words of that royal seer who had lost his memory, Budha replied with gentle, reassuring speech.

sanskrit: aśmavarṣeṇa mahatā bhṛtyās te vinipātitāḥ tvaṃ cāśramapade supto vātavarṣabhayārditaḥ
english: "Your retainers were struck down by a great shower of stones, and you fell asleep in this hermitage, afflicted by fear of the wind and rain."

sanskrit: samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te nirbhayo vigatajvaraḥ phalamūlāśano vīra vasa ceha yathāsukham
english: "Be reassured; good fortune to you — be without fear, free of grief. Live here, O hero, eating fruit and roots, at your ease."

sanskrit: sa rājā tena vākyena pratyāśvasto mahāyaśāḥ pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ dīno bhṛtyajanakṣayāt
english: Reassured by those words, that king of great renown replied with gentle words, yet grieved at the loss of his retainers.

sanskrit: tyakṣyāmy ahaṃ svakaṃ rājyaṃ nāhaṃ bhṛtyair vinā kṛtaḥ vartayeyaṃ kṣaṇaṃ brahman samanujñātum arhasi
english: "I shall abandon my own kingdom; I cannot endure even a moment without my retainers. O Brahmin, you should permit me to depart."

sanskrit: suto dharmaparo brahmañ jyeṣṭho mama mahāyaśāḥ śaśabindur iti khyātaḥ sa me rājyaṃ prapatsyate
english: "My eldest son, devoted to righteousness and of great renown, O Brahmin, known as Śaśabindu — let him receive my kingdom."

sanskrit: na hi śakṣyāmy ahaṃ gatvā bhṛtyadārān sukhānvitān prativaktuṃ mahātejaḥ kiṃ cid apy aśubhaṃ vacaḥ
english: "For I could not bear to go and speak any ill word to my retainers' wives who live in comfort, O great and radiant one."

sanskrit: tathā bruvati rājendre budhaḥ paramam adbhutam sāntvapūrvam athovāca vāsas ta iha rocatām
english: While the lord of kings spoke thus, Budha said something most wondrous by way of consolation: "Let your dwelling here be pleasing to you."

sanskrit: na saṃtāpas tvayā kāryaḥ kārdameya mahābala saṃvatsaroṣitasyeha kārayiṣyāmi te hitam
english: "You must not grieve, O son of Kardama, O great and mighty one. After you have dwelt here a full year, I will accomplish what is beneficial for you."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā budhasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ vāsāya vidadhe buddhiṃ yad uktaṃ brahmavādinā
english: Hearing those words of Budha of untiring deeds, the king resolved to remain, as the expounder of sacred knowledge had said.

sanskrit: māsaṃ sa strī tadā bhūtvā ramayaty aniśaṃ śubhā māsaṃ puruṣabhāvena dharmabuddhiṃ cakāra saḥ
english: For one month he would become a beautiful woman and take pleasure without cease; for one month he would take on the form of a man and turn his mind to dharma.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa navame māsi ilā somasutātmajam janayām āsa suśroṇī purūravasam ātmajam
english: Then, in the ninth month, the fair-hipped Ilā gave birth to a son — Purūravas — begotten by the son of Soma.

sanskrit: jātamātraṃ tu suśroṇī pitur haste nyaveśayat budhasya samavarṇābham ilāputraṃ mahābalam
english: No sooner was he born than the fair-hipped one placed him in his father's hands — that mighty son of Ilā, equal in complexion to Budha.

sanskrit: budho 'pi puruṣībhūtaṃ samāśvāsya narādhipam kathābhī ramayām āsa dharmayuktābhir ātmavān
english: Budha, self-possessed, also comforted the king when he had resumed his male form, entertaining him with stories full of righteousness.

sanskrit: tathoktavati rāme tu tasya janma tad adbhutam uvāca lakṣmaṇo bhūyo bharataś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: While Rāma spoke thus of that wondrous birth, Lakṣmaṇa and the greatly renowned Bharata spoke up again.

sanskrit: sā priyā somaputrasya saṃvatsaram athoṣitā akarot kiṃ naraśreṣṭha tat tvaṃ śaṃsitum arhasi
english: "Having dwelt a full year as the beloved of the son of Soma, what did she do, O best of men? You should relate that to us."

sanskrit: tayos tad vākyamādhuryaṃ niśamya paripṛcchatoḥ rāmaḥ punar uvācemāṃ prajāpatisute kathām
english: Listening to the sweetness of those words from the two who questioned him, Rāma then narrated this story about the daughter of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: puruṣatvaṃ gate śūre budhaḥ paramabuddhimān saṃvartaṃ paramodāram ājuhāva mahāyaśāḥ
english: When the hero had passed into the state of manhood, Budha of supreme intelligence and great renown summoned the supremely noble Saṃvarta.

sanskrit: cyavanaṃ bhṛguputraṃ ca muniṃ cāriṣṭaneminam pramodanaṃ modakaraṃ tato durvāsasaṃ munim
english: And also Cyavana, the son of Bhṛgu, and the sage Āriṣṭanemi, and Pramodana the gladdener, and then the sage Durvāsas.

sanskrit: etān sarvān samānīya vākyajñas tattvadarśinaḥ uvāca sarvān suhṛdo dhairyeṇa susamāhitaḥ
english: Having assembled all of them — skilled in speech and seers of truth — he addressed all his friends with composure and steadiness of mind.

sanskrit: ayaṃ rājā mahābāhuḥ kardamasya ilaḥ sutaḥ jānītainaṃ yathā bhūtaṃ śreyo hy asya vidhīyatām
english: "This great-armed king is Ila, the son of Kardama. Know his true situation and let what is beneficial for him be arranged."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃvadatām eva tam āśramam upāgamat kardamaḥ sumahātejā dvijaiḥ saha mahātmabhiḥ
english: Even as they were conversing, Kardama of immense splendor came to that hermitage together with great-souled twice-born sages.

sanskrit: pulastyaś ca kratuś caiva vaṣaṭkāras tathaiva ca oṃkāraś ca mahātejās tam āśramam upāgaman
english: Pulastya, Kratu, Vaṣaṭkāra, and the greatly splendid Oṃkāra also came to that hermitage.

sanskrit: te sarve hṛṣṭamanasaḥ parasparasamāgame hitaiṣiṇo bāhli pateḥ pṛthag vākyam athābruvan
english: All of them, their minds gladdened at meeting one another, well-wishers of the lord of Bāhli, then each spoke separately.

sanskrit: kardamas tv abravīd vākyaṃ sutārthaṃ paramaṃ hitam dvijāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ yac chreyaḥ pārthivasya hi
english: But Kardama spoke words supremely beneficial for the sake of his son: "O twice-born ones, hear my words, for they are what is best for the king."

sanskrit: nānyaṃ paśyāmi bhaiṣajyam antareṇa vṛṣadhvajam nāśvamedhāt paro yajñaḥ priyaś caiva mahātmanaḥ
english: "I see no remedy except the Lord whose banner bears the bull; and no sacrifice is higher than the Aśvamedha, which is also dear to that great-souled one."

sanskrit: tasmād yajāmahe sarve pārthivārthe durāsadam kardamenaivam uktās tu sarva eva dvijarṣabhāḥ rocayanti sma taṃ yajñaṃ rudrasyārādhanaṃ prati
english: "Therefore let us all perform that most formidable sacrifice for the sake of the king." Thus addressed by Kardama, all the foremost of the twice-born approved of that sacrifice as a means of propitiating Rudra.

sanskrit: saṃvartasya tu rājarṣiḥ śiṣyaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ marutta iti vikhyātas taṃ yajñaṃ samupāharat
english: The royal seer Marutta, conqueror of enemy citadels, the disciple of Saṃvarta and renowned by that name, then brought forward the materials for that sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato yajño mahān āsīd budhāśramasamīpataḥ rudraś ca paramaṃ toṣam ājagāma mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then a great sacrifice was performed near the hermitage of Budha, and Rudra of great renown came, filled with supreme satisfaction.

sanskrit: atha yajñasamāptau tu prītaḥ paramayā mudā umāpatir dvijān sarvān uvācedam ilāṃ prati
english: Then, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, the lord of Umā, pleased and filled with the greatest joy, spoke thus to all the twice-born regarding Ilā.

sanskrit: prīto 'smi hayamedhena bhaktyā ca dvijasattamāḥ asya bāhlipateś caiva kiṃ karomi priyaṃ śubham
english: "I am delighted by the Hayamedha and by your devotion, O best of the twice-born. What good and pleasing thing shall I do for this lord of Bāhli?"

sanskrit: tathā vadati deveśe dvijās te susamāhitāḥ prasādayanti deveśaṃ yathā syāt puruṣas tv ilā
english: While the lord of the gods spoke thus, those twice-born with concentrated minds propitiated the lord of the gods so that Ilā might become a man.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanā rudraḥ puruṣatvaṃ dadau punaḥ ilāyai sumahātejā dattvā cāntaradhīyata
english: Then Rudra, his heart delighted, of immense splendor, bestowed manhood once more upon Ilā, and having given this boon, vanished from sight.

sanskrit: nivṛtte hayamedhe tu gate cādarśanaṃ hare yathāgataṃ dvijāḥ sarve agacchan dīrghadarśinaḥ
english: When the Hayamedha was concluded and Hara had disappeared, all those far-sighted twice-born returned whence they had come.

sanskrit: rājā tu bāhlim utsṛjya madhyadeśe hy anuttamam niveśayām āsa puraṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ yaśaskaram
english: The king, abandoning Bāhli, established a city renowned for its glory, Pratiṣṭhāna, in the most excellent Madhyadeśa.

sanskrit: śaśabindus tu rājāsīd bāhlyāṃ parapuraṃjayaḥ pratiṣṭhāna ilo rājā prajāpatisuto balī
english: Śaśabindu, conqueror of enemy citadels, became king in Bāhli, while the mighty Ila, son of Prajāpati, became king at Pratiṣṭhāna.

sanskrit: sa kāle prāptavāṃl lokam ilo brāhmam anuttamam ailaḥ purūravā rājā pratiṣṭhānam avāptavān
english: Ila in due time attained the unsurpassed world of Brahmā, and the king Purūravas, son of Ila, obtained Pratiṣṭhāna.

sanskrit: īdṛśo hy aśvamedhasya prabhāvaḥ puruṣarṣabhau strībhūtaḥ pauruṣaṃ lebhe yac cānyad api durlabham
english: "Such indeed is the power of the Aśvamedha, O you two bulls among men: one who had become a woman thereby regained manhood — and other boons difficult to obtain besides."
